Overview

Antwerp as a Business Centre

Antwerp is Flanders' largest city and the commercial centre of the province of Antwerp. Its port, merged with Zeebrugge as Port of Antwerp-Bruges, handled 278 million tonnes of cargo in 2024, with container volumes up about 8 percent and a market share of around 30 percent in the Hamburg-Le Havre range. The port area also hosts one of the largest integrated chemicals and petrochemicals clusters in Europe. The city has long been a global centre of rough and polished diamond trading, concentrated in the diamond district near Antwerp Central station. Logistics, freight forwarding, shipping services, commodity storage and trade finance support these activities, and Dutch is the language of administration and the courts.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Antwerp because high-value goods and high-volume flows pass through it. Shippers, insurers and terminal operators face cargo theft, misdeclaration and contamination of legitimate containers by drug traffickers: Belgian customs seized a record 121 tonnes of cocaine at the port in 2023, and criminal groups seek insiders in logistics chains. Diamond buyers, banks and jewellers need assurance on counterparties and provenance, particularly since sanctions restrict trade in Russian-origin stones. Commodity traders and lenders need to know who owns warehoused goods. Insolvencies and commercial disputes before the Antwerp enterprise court generate further demand for factual research.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Antwerp

01

Logistics and freight counterparty checks

Forwarders, hauliers, warehouse operators and customs agents around the port vary widely in substance. We research ownership, directors, insolvency history and links between companies through Belgian and foreign records, helping shippers and insurers assess counterparties before contracts or after losses.

02

Cargo integrity and insider risk

Drug traffickers use legitimate containers and seek insiders in port logistics. Working with counsel and the client's security function, we review backgrounds of contractors and intermediaries, map corporate links, and support internal inquiries, leaving criminal matters to Belgian authorities.

03

Diamond trade counterparty diligence

Banks, jewellers and buyers dealing with Antwerp diamond traders need to know ownership, trading history and links to restricted jurisdictions. We research corporate structures, litigation, sanctions exposure and media across Belgium, India, the UAE and other trading centres to support provenance and compliance decisions.

04

Commodity and warehouse ownership

Lenders and traders financing goods stored in Antwerp warehouses need confidence that the goods exist and belong to the borrower. We research warehouse operators, collateral managers and counterparties, and trace related companies, to help test title and identify overlapping pledges or fraud indicators.

05

Insolvency and enforcement support

The Antwerp enterprise court supervises insolvency and company dissolution across Antwerp and Limburg. We support creditors and their Belgian counsel with research on directors, related companies and assets in Belgium and abroad, helping assess director liability claims and recovery prospects.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Antwerp

Enterprise Court of Antwerp

The Ondernemingsrechtbank Antwerpen covers the judicial arrondissements of Antwerp and Limburg, with divisions in Antwerp, Mechelen, Turnhout, Hasselt and Tongeren-Borgloon. It hears disputes between enterprises and supervises insolvency, including prevention and bankruptcy, and company register matters such as dissolution and liquidation. It also appoints liquidators of shipowners' limitation funds. Summary proceedings for the Antwerp arrondissement are centralised in the Antwerp division. Proceedings are in Dutch.

Court of Appeal and criminal courts

Appeals from the enterprise court and the Court of First Instance of Antwerp go to the Court of Appeal of Antwerp, whose territory covers the provinces of Antwerp and Limburg. Large drug trafficking and organised crime cases connected to the port are prosecuted in Antwerp, and court judgments and press coverage of these cases can be relevant sources when assessing logistics counterparties and individuals.

Port and customs environment

Port of Antwerp-Bruges operates as a public limited company owned by the cities of Antwerp and Bruges. Belgian customs handles inspections and drug seizures at the port, which fell from a record 121 tonnes in 2023 to about 22 tonnes in the first half of 2024. Access controls and certified container pick-up systems affect how logistics companies operate and what records exist.

Diamond sector and sanctions

Antwerp's diamond trade is organised around the diamond district and its bourses, with the Antwerp World Diamond Centre representing the sector. EU and G7 restrictions on Russian-origin diamonds have increased provenance and traceability requirements for traders. Diligence on diamond counterparties therefore combines Belgian corporate records with sanctions screening and research in other trading centres. TDSC screens every engagement for sanctions compliance.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Antwerp

TDSC has no office in Antwerp and works on Antwerp matters from Nashville. We agree the purpose with the client's Belgian counsel first, whether a logistics or warehouse counterparty, a diamond trader, a cargo loss or insider concern, or an insolvency, and scope the research to it. Sources include the Crossroads Bank for Enterprises, Belgian Official Gazette publications, published judgments, sanctions lists, media in Dutch, French and English, and records in other jurisdictions where counterparties are based. Belgium licenses private investigators, so any fieldwork in Antwerp is carried out by appropriately licensed Belgian professionals, and personal data is handled under the GDPR. Reports identify sources and confidence levels.

TDSC has no office in Antwerp. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Antwerp: Frequently Asked Questions

Can TDSC investigate a cargo theft or drug contamination at the port of Antwerp?

We support clients and their Belgian counsel with background and corporate research on forwarders, hauliers, contractors and intermediaries connected to a loss or incident. Criminal investigation is for Belgian police, customs and prosecutors. Any fieldwork in Belgium is carried out by licensed Belgian investigators, and research stays within lawful sources and the GDPR.

How do you check an Antwerp diamond trader?

We identify the company's directors, shareholders where available and related entities through Belgian and foreign records, then review litigation, insolvency, sanctions exposure and media in Belgium and other trading centres such as India and the UAE. Findings support counterparty, provenance and compliance decisions. Gemological questions are for specialist laboratories.

Which court handles commercial disputes and insolvency in Antwerp?

The Enterprise Court of Antwerp hears disputes between enterprises and supervises insolvency and company dissolution for the Antwerp and Limburg arrondissements, through divisions including Antwerp, Mechelen, Turnhout, Hasselt and Tongeren-Borgloon. Appeals go to the Court of Appeal of Antwerp. Proceedings are conducted in Dutch. Published judgments and Official Gazette notices can be useful research sources.

Can you verify goods held in an Antwerp warehouse?

We research the warehouse operator, collateral manager and counterparties, their ownership and history, and links between them, and coordinate licensed local professionals where a physical inspection is needed. Inspections and access depend on the operator's cooperation and the client's contractual rights, which counsel should confirm before work begins.

In which language will Antwerp records and proceedings be?

Antwerp is in the Dutch-speaking Flemish Region, so court proceedings, many official publications and local media are in Dutch. Shipping and diamond trading documents are often in English. TDSC works with sources in Dutch, French and English and can provide English summaries of Dutch-language material for clients and counsel.
